headline: Chicago November ferrous scrap settles higher: shred up $30, busheling up $20
detail: Mills paid $20-30/gt more for November scrap. In Chicago, shredded rose $30/gt and busheling $20/gt, and P&S and rail grades stayed short. Firm mill demand and slow inbound flows are holding Midwest scrap up going into winter.

headline: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee calls October inflation borderline disturbing
detail: Goolsbee said inflation is speeding up and spreading and would not rule out a half-point hike in December. A more hawkish Fed lifts the dollar, which weighs on copper, aluminum and gold.

headline: LME aluminum stocks sink to lowest since 1990, squeezing cash prices
detail: Exchange aluminum stocks fell to a 35-year low and cash metal jumped to a premium of roughly $150/t over three-month, with a couple of traders reportedly holding much of the available metal. That squeeze, not new demand, drove Wednesday's jump in cash aluminum.

headline: Copper bounces back as China runs short of metal
detail: Three-month LME copper rose about 0.8% Wednesday after Tuesday's CPI selloff, helped by better tech sentiment. China's import premium held at a record for a third day, showing physical tightness that is cushioning prices against the strong dollar.

headline: Gold drops below $4,000 as the dollar hits its highest since spring 2025
detail: Gold fell about 1% late Wednesday as the dollar index climbed near 103 and futures priced a December rate hike as very likely. Silver held around $51.50.

headline: Steel buyers expect hot-rolled coil to reach $1,400-1,449 within two months
detail: A Steel Market Update survey found tight supply and steady demand keeping sheet prices climbing, with mixed views on when the rally tops out. Strong mill demand supports prime and busheling scrap.

headline: Nucor lifts HRC spot price $15 to $1,295/st, the 17th straight weekly increase
detail: Nucor raised its weekly hot-rolled coil price again, with lead times holding at 3-5 weeks. US HRC is trading about $1,340-1,400/st. Strong sheet prices keep EAF mills hungry for prime and shredded scrap.

headline: Palladium jumps about 6% to near $1,087
detail: Palladium is up roughly 16% since Nov 4 as short sellers covered and Nornickel warned of lower output in 2027-28. That helps catalytic converter values, though weak auto output and more recycling remain headwinds.

headline: US Steel and the Steelworkers resume contract talks Friday
detail: Talks restart Nov 13 after stalling; Cleveland-Cliffs already reached its deal with the union. Any strike threat at US Steel would be a wildcard for flat-rolled supply and mill scrap buying.

headline: Thailand tightens imports of copper, aluminum and steel scrap
detail: Thailand is drafting tougher impurity, certification and importer rules and has stepped up customs checks, pushing some cargoes to Malaysia and India. Fewer Asian outlets could pressure US nonferrous scrap export prices.

headline: China's copper import premiums hit record highs
detail: Shanghai import premiums passed $200/t, the highest on record, as metal is diverted to the US, smelters run maintenance and Chinese stocks shrink. SMM expects premiums to stay high through December, which supports copper prices.

headline: Strike at Teck's Highland Valley copper mine nears three weeks
detail: More than 1,200 Steelworkers have been out since Oct 24 at the British Columbia mine, and tensions are rising over replacement workers. It adds to an already tight copper concentrate market.

headline: Fed's Waller says a half-point December hike should be on the table
detail: Fed Governor Waller said a 25bp hike could put the Fed's credibility at risk if core inflation stays hot. A larger hike would support the dollar and tighten credit for metal buyers and end users.

headline: Importers press for $166 billion in refunds of struck-down tariffs
detail: A class of importers asked the trade court to order refunds of the IEEPA tariffs, with the Justice Department's answer due Nov 13. The Section 232 steel, aluminum and copper tariffs are not affected.

headline: US and China extend their trade truce two more months, to January 10
detail: China paused some critical-mineral export controls and its 24% tariff on US goods for two more months, though a 10% duty remains. The US extended 178 Section 301 tariff exclusions on Chinese goods. This avoids a near-term escalation that could have rattled metals markets and supply chains.

headline: China's central bank promises more support for the economy
detail: The PBoC said it will keep policy loose and borrowing costs low, with more lending for consumer demand and infrastructure. Stimulus hopes support base metal demand.

headline: China's October steel exports fall 6% from September
detail: China shipped 9.85 Mt of steel in October as a new export license system holds volumes back. Less cheap Chinese steel abroad supports steel prices outside China.

headline: Nickel slips as Treasury yields and the dollar climb
detail: Shanghai nickel eased as the 10-year Treasury yield neared 5% after the hot CPI report. SMM sees a sideways range unless producers follow through on announced output cuts.

headline: Midterm results raise hopes of Canada tariff relief that could shrink the Midwest premium
detail: The Midwest aluminum premium had eased to $1.12/lb from a record $1.19 in May. After Democratic wins, traders expect pressure for a US-Canada deal on the 50% tariff. Any decline is expected to be gradual, but scrap brokers cut prices quickly the last time a deal was floated.

headline: Kazakhstan bans scrap exports for six months
detail: The ban, in force since Nov 1, covers ferrous, nonferrous and stainless scrap to keep material for local mills. It trims supply in world scrap trade.

headline: New-car prices hit a record $51,109 as dealer inventory climbs to 3.1 million
detail: Inventory rose by about 100,000 units while prices stayed high. Fuller lots point to softer production ahead, which means less prompt industrial scrap from auto plants.

headline: Ford's October US sales slip 0.8%
detail: F-Series pickups and big SUVs gained while overall Ford sales dipped slightly; used wholesale prices are up about 2% from a year ago. Flat sales keep auto steel and aluminum demand steady but not growing.

headline: Stellantis keeps Windsor minivan and Charger plant down for a fourth straight week
detail: Production at Windsor Assembly, which has about 6,400 workers, is idled through the week of Nov 9, and Stellantis cites demand and tariffs. Long shutdowns cut flat-rolled steel and aluminum demand and the flow of prompt industrial scrap from feeder plants.

headline: Platinum holds near $1,540 close to a two-week high
detail: Rate-hike bets and weak auto output weigh on platinum, but demand from hybrids and catalytic converters is cushioning the dip.

headline: Sibanye-Stillwater cuts US PGM output forecast after Montana strike
detail: Sibanye lowered 2026 output from its Montana mines to 245,000-255,000 oz, from 280,000-300,000 oz, after a five-week strike, and raised its cost guidance. Less US-mined palladium and platinum lends some support to PGM prices.

headline: Standard Chartered still sees gold at $4,650 this quarter
detail: The bank expects one December hike then a pause and points to strong ETF and central bank buying. It sees $4,200 as the next hurdle.

headline: Nonresidential construction forecast to grow only about 2% in 2027
detail: Data centers and power projects keep growing while chip plants, warehouses and public work fall. That is mixed for rebar, structural steel and copper wire demand.

headline: Mortgage rates post biggest one-day jump in over a month after CPI
detail: The average 30-year fixed rate rose to about 7.30%, up 0.12 point in a day after the hot inflation report. Higher borrowing costs further cool homebuilding and the demand for wire, pipe and rebar that comes with it.

headline: Codelco cuts 2026 copper guidance to about 1.2 Mt and admits overstating past output
detail: Chile's state miner lowered its 2026 target from 1.34 Mt. It confirmed that 42,100 t of 2024-25 output was overstated and dropped its goal of 1.7 Mt a year by 2030. Lower supply from the world's top copper producer supports copper prices over the longer term.

headline: Nickel jumps to five-week high as Indonesia cracks down on a major ore trader
detail: LME nickel rose 3.8% to $16,375/t after Indonesia's forestry task force moved against firms tied to a large nickel ore trader. Tighter Indonesian supply can support nickel and stainless scrap values.
